issues.description: Field mismatch for Person.id: the template/common model and the problem endpoints imply UUID identifiers (template's src/common/.../Person.java declares 'private UUID id;' and the REST endpoints in the problem statement use {personId} path variables), and the solution server code treats IDs as UUIDs (e.g., PersonService calls person.setId(UUID.randomUUID()) and PersonResource uses @PathVariable UUID personId). However, the solution's common Person model declares the id field as Long (private Long id;). This inconsistent type for the same conceptual attribute 'Person.id' (UUID vs Long) will cause compilation errors (e.g., calling person.setId(UUID.randomUUID()) when setId expects Long) and will confuse students about the correct identifier type to use across client, common, and server layers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id type consistent across all artifacts. The recommended fix (keeps problem statement and server code intact) is to modify the common Person model used by both client and server to declare id as java.util.UUID (change field, getter, and setter to use UUID). Ensure all usage sites (client controller, server service, and resource) treat id as UUID. Alternatively, if Long is preferred, change the server resource and service signatures and ID generation to use Long consistently (and update problem statement examples), but do not mix UUID and Long for the same attribute.
